question_text: How many seconds are in 2 hours?

hint_ladder.title: 1 oras = ilang segundo?
hint_ladder.text: 1 oras = 60 minutes x 60 seconds = 3,600 seconds. Basic ito.

hint_ladder.title: Multiply mo sa 2
hint_ladder.text: Dahil 2 oras ang tanong, i-multiply ang 3,600 sa 2. Parang pagbili ng dalawang kilo ng bigas.

hint_ladder.title: Sagot: 7,200
hint_ladder.text: Kaya 2 oras = 7,200 segundo. Tama ang sagot na C.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you only got seconds for 1 hour, forgetting to multiply by 2. 3,600 is for isang oras lang.

B.text: You might have chosen B because you miscalculated, maybe 1.5 hours instead of 2, or used a wrong base conversion.

C.text: Correct. 2 hours × 60 minutes × 60 seconds = 7,200 seconds. Basic conversion lang.

D.text: You might have chosen D because you doubled the correct answer, perhaps multiplying 3,600 by 4 instead of 2.

next_time_rule: To convert hours to seconds: multiply hours by 3,600. For 2 hours, 2 × 3,600 = 7,200. Isipin mo lang 'hours × 3,600'.
deconstruct_text:
Imagine riding a jeepney from Cubao to Quiapo—your trip takes exactly 2 hours. You want to know how many seconds you're on that vehicle. Simple lang: just convert hours to seconds with basic math.

1 hour = 60 minutes, and 1 minute = 60 seconds. So 1 hour = 60 × 60 = 3,600 seconds. Since you're on the road for 2 hours, multiply: 2 × 3,600 = 7,200 seconds. That's how long you'll be enjoying the jeepney ride!

Mental Trick: Parang sa palengke: 1 kilo ng bigas = 3,600 piso? Hindi, pero 1 oras = 3,600 seconds. Kaya 2 oras, doblehin mo lang. Slogan: 'Oras times 3,600.' Kasing-dali lang!

Distractor Alert: A (3,600) ay pang-isang oras lang—nalimutan i-multiply. B (5,400) parang 1.5 oras, maling conversion. D (14,400) sobra, baka na-multiply sa 4 imbes na 2.
